data.topic: portable per-project AI decision memory: vector-backed decision tracking for legacy codebases that auto-discovers implicit architectural decisions, stores them with file-level associations in a portable embedded database, and dynamically injects relevant context at edit time

findings.summary: Two separate decision storage systems already exist: decisions table (epics.db) for explicit architectural decisions, and decision_preferences table (epics.db) for behavioral decision tracking with signal scoring
findings.details: The decisions table stores title/chose/rejected/reasoning with file/pattern/tech scopes via decision_scopes junction table. decision_preferences tracks routing/scope/communication/architecture decisions with signal_score/signal_count for correction correlation. These are complementary but disconnected systems — decisions are explicitly recorded via pm_add_decision, while decision_preferences are auto-correlated with user corrections via signal_processor.py.

findings.summary: OpenMemory is the existing semantic memory layer — Node.js MCP server backed by openmemory.sqlite with Ollama embeddings, user_id scoping, and sector-based organization
findings.details: OpenMemory runs as a separate Node.js MCP server (~/.claude/.claude/openmemory-server/) communicating via stdio. Uses sqlite3 (Node) for metadata and vectors. Embeddings via Ollama nomic-embed-text. Supports HSG (hierarchical semantic graph) queries with sector filtering (episodic, semantic, procedural, emotional, reflective). All writes from Python hooks route through om_write.py which enforces tag whitelist, dedup (0.85 cosine), per-category budgets, and decay-weighted pruning.

findings.summary: Decision shadow writes already bridge epics.db decisions to OpenMemory via om_write() with 'decision' tag and semantic sector
findings.details: tools_knowledge.py:_om_shadow_decision() calls om_write() after every pm_add_decision, storing '[decision-ID] title: chose X. reasoning' with tags=['decision'], user_id='proj:dotclaude', sector='semantic', decay_lambda=0.01. This gives decisions semantic search capability via OpenMemory queries. Budget is 50 decision entries.

findings.summary: Embedding utilities are centralized in hooks/lib/embedding_utils.py — single source of truth per decision-105
findings.details: get_embedding() calls Ollama nomic-embed-text at localhost:11434/api/embeddings. Returns 768d float vectors. Utility functions: cosine_similarity(), embedding_to_blob() (struct.pack little-endian float32), blob_to_embedding(). MCP server imports via sys.path manipulation (server.py adds project root to sys.path).

findings.summary: Context injection follows a three-tier architecture per decision-66: SessionStart always, UserPromptSubmit keyword-triggered, async background
findings.details: Tier 1: load-session-context.sh runs at session start — loads CLAUDE.md, ORCHESTRATION.md, renders behavioral prefs from correction_groups DB, queries top 5 tool-learnings from OpenMemory, computes trust scores, shows session agenda. Tier 2: inject-tier2-context.sh fires on UserPromptSubmit, matches keywords (story-NNN, epics.db, openmemory, hook, worktree, etc.) and injects targeted context fragments. Max 3 injections per session. Tier 3: background async processing.

findings.summary: MCP server registration pattern: FastMCP with modular tool registration via register(mcp) functions in separate files
findings.details: server.py creates FastMCP('gemini'), then imports register functions from each tools_*.py module and calls them with the mcp instance. Each module defines tools via @mcp.tool() decorator. DB access through _db_op() context manager with WAL mode, busy_timeout=3000, foreign_keys=ON. Schema migrations run once at server startup via startup_migrate().

findings.summary: Current embedding stack requires Ollama running locally — no fallback for embeddings, only simhash fallback for dedup
findings.details: decision-74 explicitly chose 'no regex fallback if Ollama unavailable' for correction detection. om_write.py falls back to MD5 simhash for dedup only when Ollama is down, but stores no embedding vector. OpenMemory queries return empty when Ollama is unreachable. The session start hook warns about this but doesn't block.

findings.summary: Memory infrastructure reduced to 3 persistence surfaces per decision-79: correction_groups (epics.db), rendered-prefs.md (sidecar), openmemory.sqlite
findings.details: Four surfaces were killed (corrections.md, correction-tallies.jsonl, om-ops.json, tool-learnings.md). Adding a new persistence surface contradicts this consolidation decision. Any new portable decision DB would be surface #4 unless it replaces or subsumes one of the existing three.

findings.summary: All OpenMemory writes must go through om_write.py — tag whitelist, dedup, and budget enforcement are mandatory
findings.details: ALLOWED_TAGS: behavioral-pref, tool-learning, decision, prompt-pattern, session-summary, critique-learning, gemini-blind-spot. Adding a new tag requires updating: om_write.py ALLOWED_TAGS, BUDGETS, CLAUDE.md integration surfaces, and refs/orch-memory.md. Direct INSERT into the memories table is prohibited per decision-104.

findings.summary: Python MCP server uses Python 3.11 with mcp>=1.26.0, standard lib sqlite3, and Ollama for embeddings
findings.details: requirements.txt is minimal: mcp>=1.26.0, uvicorn, pytest. All embedding work uses stdlib urllib for Ollama HTTP calls. OpenMemory server is Node.js (openmemory-js v1.3.3) with sqlite3 v5.1.7. No sqlite-vec, fastembed, or ONNX dependencies exist anywhere in the project today.

findings.summary: Existing decision schema in epics.db has file-level scope associations via decision_scopes but no vector embeddings
findings.details: decisions table: id, title, chose, rejected, reasoning, status, decided_at, superseded_by, story_id. decision_scopes: decision_id, scope_type (file|pattern|tech), scope_value. No embedding column, no vector index. Semantic search goes through OpenMemory shadow copies, not the decisions table directly.

findings.summary: Test patterns: pytest with subprocess execution for integration tests, tmp_path fixtures, sqlite3 direct assertions
findings.details: Tests in .claude/tests/ use pytest. Pattern: subprocess.run the script, assert returncode, parse JSON stdout, verify SQLite state via direct connection. GitFixture class creates bare+worktree repos for integration tests. No mocking of Ollama or embedding calls in existing tests.

findings.summary: The project is a user-scoped Claude Code orchestration system (~/.claude/), not a standalone library — portability means working across projects the user opens
findings.details: Everything lives under ~/.claude/ and is registered via Claude Code MCP configuration and hooks (settings.json). Per-project scoping exists via user_id='proj:<name>' in OpenMemory. The decision memory currently lives in a single epics.db that mixes cross-project infrastructure (correction_groups, decision_preferences) with project-specific data (stories, epics, tasks). Making decisions truly per-project-portable means either: (a) a per-project .decisions.db file discoverable from any project root, or (b) user_id-scoped partitions in the existing centralized stores.

decisions_relevant.summary: Embedding logic consolidated via sys.path import — MCP server imports from hooks.lib.embedding_utils
decisions_relevant.impact: Any new embedding code must use hooks/lib/embedding_utils.py as the single source of truth. Cannot introduce a parallel embedding module.

decisions_relevant.summary: Shadow decision writes route through om_write() — no direct INSERT into memories table
decisions_relevant.impact: All semantic memory writes must go through om_write.py. A portable per-project DB would need its own write gate or extend om_write.

decisions_relevant.summary: Memory infrastructure reduced to 3 persistence surfaces
decisions_relevant.impact: Adding a new .db file is surface #4 — must justify why it can't be folded into existing surfaces. Strong preference for extending over adding.

decisions_relevant.summary: Correction detection uses semantic delta via Ollama nomic-embed-text, no fallback
decisions_relevant.impact: Establishes that Ollama dependency is accepted. FastEmbed/ONNX alternative from research would be a new dependency contradicting the accepted Ollama-only pattern.
Edit-time decision injection must fit into this tiered model — likely Tier 2 (keyword-triggered) or a new MCP tool query. Cannot add a Tier 1 (always-load) decision dump.

decisions_relevant.summary: Behavioral prefs use dynamic sidecar file via @import for compaction resilience
decisions_relevant.impact: Established pattern for session-start context: render from DB to sidecar file, load via @import. Per-project decision context could follow the same pattern.

decisions_relevant.summary: Memory snapshot dedup: dropped behavioral-pref from session-start OpenMemory query, kept only tool-learnings
decisions_relevant.impact: Precedent against loading all decisions at session start. Decision memory injection must be selective/on-demand.

decisions_relevant.summary: Async Stop hook via background subprocess for slow operations
decisions_relevant.impact: Pattern for decision discovery: heavy LLM-based analysis of code should run in background stop hook, not block session operations.

decisions_relevant.summary: Graduated autonomy with layered trust — global baseline + domain overrides
decisions_relevant.impact: Establishes pattern for per-domain scoping. Per-project decision memory follows same pattern: global decisions + project-scoped overrides.

conflicts.subject: Embedding runtime: Ollama vs FastEmbed/ONNX
conflicts.codebase_says: All embedding operations use Ollama nomic-embed-text via HTTP API (decision-74, decision-105). No ONNX, no FastEmbed. Accepted dependency with 'no fallback if unavailable' policy.
conflicts.research_says: FastEmbed (ONNX Runtime) enables serverless embedding without Ollama — ~15ms/chunk on CPU, fully offline after model download. Recommended for portability.
conflicts.resolution: Codebase wins for the orchestration project. FastEmbed is relevant only if building a standalone portable library intended for machines without Ollama. For this project's per-project decision memory, Ollama is the established embedding provider. If portability to Ollama-free environments is a goal, FastEmbed would require a new decision superseding decision-74.

conflicts.subject: sqlite-vec for vector search vs current BLOB + Python cosine
conflicts.codebase_says: Embeddings stored as raw float32 BLOBs in openmemory.sqlite memories table. Similarity computed in Python (cosine_similarity in embedding_utils.py). No native vector indexing. Works for <1000 entries.
conflicts.research_says: sqlite-vec provides native vector search in SQLite — sub-75ms at 100k vectors, binary quantization for 10x speedup. Required for scaling beyond a few hundred entries.
conflicts.resolution: Research wins if decision count per project exceeds ~500. Current Python brute-force is fine for the existing ~50-entry decision budget. sqlite-vec becomes necessary if the portable DB is intended to hold code-chunk embeddings (thousands) alongside decisions. Add sqlite-vec as an optional dependency — use it when available, fall back to Python cosine for small datasets.

conflicts.subject: Separate per-project .db file vs centralized store with user_id partitioning
conflicts.codebase_says: All memory in centralized openmemory.sqlite with user_id='proj:<name>' scoping. decision-79 limits to 3 persistence surfaces. Adding a 4th .db is a policy violation.
conflicts.research_says: A single portable .db file per project (committed to repo or in .claude/) is the key to cross-tool portability. Continue.dev and Cursor both use per-project indexes.
conflicts.resolution: Tension is real. For pure cross-tool portability (Cursor/Windsurf reading the same DB), a standalone per-project file wins. For internal consistency, extending the existing centralized stores wins. Recommend: per-project .decisions.db file that is optionally importable into OpenMemory, rather than replacing OpenMemory. This adds surface #4 but the new surface lives in the target project's repo, not in ~/.claude/.

conflicts.subject: Auto-discovery of implicit decisions from code behavior
conflicts.codebase_says: No mechanism for auto-discovering decisions from code. All decisions are explicitly recorded via pm_add_decision. The codebase has no AST analysis, no commit parsing, no SATD detection.
conflicts.research_says: Auto-discovery is a confirmed research gap — 44% false positive rate, no published end-to-end system. Multi-stage pipeline (SATD + commits + LLM synthesis) is untested.
conflicts.resolution: Both agree this is novel and hard. Codebase has no foundation for it. If pursued, it should be a separate feature with human-in-the-loop validation, not an automatic pipeline. Start with explicit decision recording + edit-time injection, add auto-discovery later as an optional enrichment step.

conflicts.subject: 256d Matryoshka vs full 768d embeddings
conflicts.codebase_says: embedding_utils.py returns whatever nomic-embed-text produces — currently 768d vectors. No truncation, no dimension selection. BLOB storage assumes full dimension.
conflicts.research_says: 256d Matryoshka embeddings give 98.8% quality at half the storage. Sweet spot for decision memory use case.
conflicts.resolution: Research is right that 256d is sufficient for decisions, but changing dimensions would break compatibility with existing OpenMemory embeddings. If building a new per-project DB from scratch, use 256d. If extending the existing system, keep 768d for compatibility unless migrating all embeddings.

gaps: No per-project decision database exists — all decisions are centralized in ~/.claude/.claude/epics.db regardless of which project they belong to
No mechanism to discover decisions when editing a file — decisions have file scopes but no query path triggered by file access
No sqlite-vec or any native vector index in the project — all similarity computed in Python brute-force
No FastEmbed or ONNX runtime — Ollama is the only embedding provider, creating a hard dependency for portability
No FTS5 (full-text search) on any decision-related table — no keyword fallback when embeddings are unavailable
No import/export mechanism for decisions — cannot move decisions between machines or projects
No auto-discovery pipeline for implicit decisions from code patterns, commits, or comments
No tests for embedding_utils.py, om_write.py, or the context injection hooks
OpenMemory Node.js server embedding logic is separate from Python embedding_utils.py — two implementations of the same Ollama API call
